markdown_report:
The best early-stage direction remains a **bounded, recent-source transition residual**, with stricter provenance and evidence controls. Benefits remain hypotheses until measured on the pinned validation benchmark.

**Insights and directions.** Three starting-point insights motivate evidence control: (1) Directed successors can distinguish specific continuations from broad similarity, but transitions cannot certify compatibility. (2) Distinct-user support reduces reliance on isolated observations, provided training labels cannot supply their own support. (3) Recent sources can reduce older-interest influence; bounding the correction protects SASRec when evidence is weak.

Three literature insights sharpen these directions: (1) [ICSRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.14318) supports history-derived intent learning without establishing purchase purpose. (2) [FPMC](https://www.ra.ethz.ch/cdstore/www2010/www/p811.pdf) already adds asymmetric transitions to personalization, limiting originality claims. Directed graph projections likewise motivate asymmetry, not proven complementarity. (3) [gSASRec](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/0939.pdf) motivates objective controls. Electronics’ 13.08% training wrong-ranking rate warrants investigation but predicts no validation gain.

**Framework.** Three axes organize comparisons: context (full history/recent suffix), relationship evidence (latent/count-supported directed), and supervision (single/multiple negatives). SASRec supplies generalization; the residual adds supported pairwise evidence. Aggregating three recent sources remains first-order pairwise scoring, not third-order modeling.

**Candidate assessments.** Scores are 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each cell provides a positive and negative reason.

| Idea | Originality | Potential | User alignment | Model alignment | Difficulty |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A: Recent, support-gated directed residual | 3: specific gate / FPMC precedent | 6: interpretable control / sparse coverage | 8: recent specific continuations / no compatibility guarantee | 7: candidate separation / uncertain gains | 6: small branch / provenance and lookup complexity |
| B: Uniform multi-negative gBCE | 3: principled control / established | 7: reusable baseline / compute cost | 4: sharper ranking / no intent mechanism | 8: weak-margin target / training metrics insufficient | 3: local change / calibration care |
| C: Scratch-trained title successor scorer | 5: directional sharing / familiar components | 6: sparse-edge sharing / weak text coverage | 6: finer associations / misleading similarity | 5: shared evidence / noise | 6: permitted inputs / encoder work |

**Select A at 10% progress.** It explicitly targets broad associations lacking specific continuation evidence and older interests dominating current direction. Candidate-specific corrections target weak positive–negative separation. It cannot identify satisfied needs.

Use the latest three sources, normalized recency weights, separate source/target embeddings, distinct-user support, and a bounded correction initialized near zero. Build counts only from training histories; subtract each training user’s entire contribution using explicit upstream user IDs. Never infer identity from padded sequences. Singleton evidence is disabled consistently; remaining count-distribution mismatch must still be measured. Save the exact inference tables and scorer.

Prioritize baseline, count-only augmentation, and learned augmentation under matched budgets; test ungated, symmetric, and objective-only controls if affordable. Select exclusively by four-category macro validation HR@10. Preserve routing, seeds, splits, predictor parity, and diagnosis contracts. Report support coverage, backbone/residual margins, category deltas, and paired-user uncertainty. One changed hit equals 0.125 macro percentage points. Bootstrap intervals exclude training randomness and selection optimism; sampled HR@10 does not establish full-catalog quality.

idea.description: Add a bounded, directed transition residual from the latest three nonpadding items to each dataset-specific SASRec scorer. Separate source and target embeddings are gated by candidate-specific distinct-user transition support. Preserve the backbone score when independent transition evidence is absent.
idea.motivation: The selected idea explicitly addresses two observed user failures: broad associations without evidence of a specific continuation, and older interests overriding a narrower recent direction. Candidate-specific corrections may address Electronics’ weak positive–negative separation, including its negative training margin p10 and 13.08% sampled wrong-ranking rate. These are hypotheses, not measured improvements. Neither observed transitions nor text similarity establish equipment compatibility, incremental usefulness, or satisfied needs. FPMC and sequential-rule precedents reduce the originality rating from 5 to 3; sparse coverage and support shift reduce future potential from 7 to 6; provenance, scoring parity, and full-catalog integration increase difficulty from 4 to 6. Objective-only gBCE remains a valuable independent control, while scratch-trained text scoring should follow evidence that sparse transition coverage is the limiting factor.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], all four categories and dataset routing, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, unchanged splits, and SASREC_EPOCHS default 200. Use a single GPU and write checkpoints, support tables, logs, and generated predictor beneath the trial directory. All training, debugging, and diagnostics count against the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. No extra datasets, pretrained weights, hidden test files, or unavailable reviews, ratings, categories, prices, stores, or simulator traits may be used.

Construct directed adjacent-transition tables from complete training histories only. Define C(s,j) as the number of distinct training users exhibiting s→j and N(s) as the number of distinct users with an outgoing adjacent transition from s. Retain each user's unique edge and source sets. For a training example belonging to u, use C_minus_u=C−1[(s,j) occurs anywhere in u's training history] and N_minus_u=N−1[s has an outgoing transition in u's history]. Because counts are distinct-user counts, repeated occurrences contribute one indicator, not their occurrence frequency. Subtract the entire user's contribution, not merely the supervised occurrence. Apply all thresholds and gates after subtraction. With baseline BCE there is no row-probability normalization; if normalized-transition controls are implemented, recompute their denominators consistently after exclusion.

Stable user provenance is mandatory upstream. Training records must retain user_id before padding/truncation and supply it explicitly to the training scorer, or contain precomputed aligned support features. Do not infer users from sequence equality or use mutable batch context. Retain the public diagnosis loader's (None, sequence, positive, negative) contract; a separate internal training collate may carry provenance. If upstream provenance cannot be supplied, the leave-user-out implementation is not reproducible and must not silently fall back to self-including counts.

For each causal position take up to three latest nonpadding sources, newest first, with weights proportional to 2^(−age), renormalized over valid sources. All three consult adjacent C_1(s,j) counts. This is recency-weighted first-order aggregation, not a joint third-order model; lag-matched C_1,C_2,C_3 would be a separate ablation. Use rank-16 source/target embeddings U,V and
r(h,j)=A * sum_s w_s * g_source(s) * g_edge(s,j) * tanh(dot(U[s],V[j])/sqrt(16)).
Set g_source=N/(N+5), g_edge=1[C>=2]*C/(C+5), A=2*sigmoid(a), and initialize a=−4. Initialize U,V independently with small nonzero random values, such as Normal(0,0.02), so neither factor blocks gradients. These are proposed fixed starting settings, not validated optima. The total correction has magnitude at most 2. Initialize no extra causal gate: the fixed recency weights and evidence gates provide a minimal first experiment. Keep the baseline architecture, loss, optimizer, sampling, and epochs unchanged initially to isolate the residual.

At inference use complete training tables with the same minimum support and gate formulas. The minimum support disables global singleton edges, but does not remove train/inference shift: an edge with two users loses support for its contributing training users and becomes active at inference. Report gate activation and count distributions under both regimes. Leave-user-out estimation prevents self-inclusion; it does not make inference counts identically distributed. A fixed reference-user partition with disjoint scorer-training users would align tables more closely, but sacrifices training data; partition ensembles cost additional budget and are a later control.

Encode sparse edge keys as int64 source*(N_items+1)+target, sort once, and register keys/counts as model buffers; use per-user sparse membership data for training subtraction. Implement torch.searchsorted with empty-table handling, safe clamping, equality masks, and zero outputs for missing or padded edges. Avoid dense catalog-squared tables. Save tables, U,V, amplitude, support constants, source window, and routing configuration. Predictor writing must load the same architecture and implement identical scores. Encode each sequence once, chunk full-catalog candidate scoring, mask seen items for simulator recommendations, and merge top-k deterministically using item ID as the secondary tie key. Do not change host candidate construction or evaluation masking.

Maintain DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions, with view.model the actual trained nn.Module. Preserve view.item_emb, user_train, meta_data, review_data, log2feats(sequence), and predict_score(features, items). To avoid hidden mutable state, define an explicit structured feature payload containing backbone states and causal recent-source IDs, and adapt probes to use it; predict_score consumes that payload for augmented scoring. If any existing caller requires a tensor feature contract, provide a separate explicit sequence-scoring adapter and update every caller consistently. Diagnosis batches without provenance can report full-count training-position margins, clearly labeled as such; they must not be represented as leave-user-out training margins. Also report backbone margins, branch magnitude, support coverage, zero-support strata, existing finite-gradient status without backward passes, and counts of evaluated positions. Do not fabricate absent recent-branch measurements. Embedding alignment alone does not establish collapse or diversity; metadata category breakdowns remain empty and review-dependent probes remain unavailable.

Before costly trials verify directionality, padding, missing and empty tables, repeated-user subtraction, causal prefixes, zero-support fallback, boundedness, serialization, and agreement between sampled and chunked scoring. Log peak memory and throughput. Use SASRec alone as the zero-residual control rather than spending a duplicate training run. Prioritize SASRec plus count-only scores and SASRec plus learned gated scores; compare ungated learned scores, symmetric evidence/factors, bounded versus unbounded scoring, and objective-only gBCE only if budget allows. Match source windows, baseline optimization, training opportunities, and GPU budgets wherever the comparison permits. A normalized-count control may use P(j|s)=(C(s,j)+alpha*p_j)/(sum_k C(s,k)+alpha), where p_j is training target popularity; identify it as an additional scorer and apply all normalization consistently. Do not interpret gains as learned generalization unless count-only and zero-count-pair behavior support that claim.

Choose exclusively using the pinned macro validation HR@10 with 200 users/category, 99 unique negatives, and evaluation seed 42. Predeclare comparisons and log every attempted trial. Where host validation outputs expose per-user hits, retain paired hit indicators on identical candidates, report per-category changes and discordant wins/losses, and bootstrap users independently within each category while recomputing the macro difference. One changed hit is 0.5 percentage points within a category and 0.125 macro points. Such intervals condition on fitted models and fixed candidates, exclude seed/candidate variability, and do not correct repeated-selection optimism. Leave confirmation to the host-held-out evaluation. Do not claim sampled-ranking improvements imply full-catalog improvements. No experiments or gains are claimed here.
idea.pseudocode:
For each of the four categories:
    retain stable user IDs in internal training records
    build distinct-user directed adjacent-edge counts C and outgoing-source counts N
    retain each user's unique edge/source membership
    initialize baseline SASRec and rank-16 directed embeddings U,V
    initialize a=-4; A_max=2; tau_source=tau_edge=5; min_support=2
    for each internal training batch with explicit user provenance:
        encode causal prefixes once
        take latest three nonpadding sources at each supervised position
        assign normalized weights proportional to 2^(-source_age)
        for each positive and sampled negative candidate:
            look up C(source,candidate), N(source)
            subtract the current user's entire distinct-user contribution
            compute thresholded support gates from adjusted counts
            add bounded recency-weighted directed residual to backbone score
        optimize unchanged baseline loss
    save model, full training tables, scoring configuration, and category routing
    write predictor with identical scoring and chunked candidate support
    run adapted diagnostics; label full-count and leave-user-out regimes distinctly
Validate scorer invariants before training costly comparisons.
Prioritize baseline, count-only augmentation, and learned augmentation at matched budgets.
Select only by pinned four-category macro validation HR@10.
Report paired validation uncertainty if per-user outputs are available; reserve held-out confirmation for the host.

originality.positive: The specific combination of distinct-user support, recent causal sources, and a bounded SASRec correction provides a focused experimental distinction.
originality.negative: FPMC already combines personalization with asymmetric transitions, and sequential rules already aggregate directed recency-weighted evidence; the gate alone does not establish substantive novelty.

future_potential.positive: Creates an interpretable setting for studying when independently supported transition evidence improves sequential ranking and when the backbone should dominate.
future_potential.negative: Sparse coverage, count-distribution shift, and uncertain correspondence between transitions and useful complementarity may limit improvements and broader impact.

code_difficulty.positive: Retains the backbone and adds a compact scoring branch using standard sparse lookup primitives.
code_difficulty.negative: Stable user provenance, leave-user-out subtraction, causal feature plumbing, diagnosis adaptation, serialization, and chunked full-catalog predictor parity require substantial care.

related_work.title: ICSRec
contributions: Learns intent representations through subsequence alignment and clustered intent prototypes.
limitations: Does not establish actual purchase purpose, satisfaction, or gains on the pinned four-category benchmark.

related_work.title: Revisiting Graph Projections
contributions: Uses directed weighted projections of user–item interactions to infer complementary relationships.
limitations: Does not establish that every sequential transition represents functional compatibility or validate the proposed distinct-user support gate.

related_work.title: gSASRec: Reducing Overconfidence in Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Motivates calibrated binary cross-entropy and increased negative sampling as controlled SASRec improvements.
limitations: Requires benchmark-specific validation and does not explicitly resolve current-intent or satisfied-need errors.

related_work.title: Factorizing Personalized Markov Chains for Next-Basket Recommendation
contributions: Combines personalization with additive directed transition factors using separate source and destination embeddings.
limitations: Does not validate this proposal's support gating, SASRec integration, or benchmark performance.

related_work.title: Evaluation of Session-Based Recommendation Algorithms
contributions: Provides sequential-rule precedents for order-sensitive, distance-weighted item relationships and motivates simple transition controls.
limitations: Pairwise transition aggregation does not establish joint higher-order modeling or functional compatibility.

related_work.title: Target Encoder's Internal Cross Fitting
contributions: Illustrates exclusion of an example's own target information when constructing predictive encoded features.
limitations: Sequential transition counts require user-level provenance and grouping beyond ordinary example-level cross-fitting.

related_work.title: GroupKFold
contributions: Supports keeping all examples from the same user together in a cross-fitting alternative.
limitations: Grouping alone does not eliminate differences between cross-fitted training support and full-table inference support.

related_work.title: CatBoost: Unbiased Boosting with Categorical Features
contributions: Analyzes prediction shift associated with target-derived features and motivates careful exclusion schemes.
limitations: Does not directly establish the best exclusion or support-alignment strategy for this sequential recommender.

related_work.title: PyTorch torch.searchsorted
contributions: Provides the sorted-key lookup primitive for sparse directed-edge buffers.
limitations: Application code must handle missing keys, padding, empty tables, bounds, and exact equality.

related_work.title: SciPy bootstrap
contributions: Provides resampling primitives for paired validation comparisons.
limitations: Stratification across categories must be implemented explicitly; ordinary bootstrap intervals do not account for model-selection optimism or training randomness.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains optimism introduced by repeated model selection on finite validation data.
limitations: Does not provide an automatic correction for this search; independent held-out confirmation remains necessary.

related_work.title: On the Bias of Offline Evaluation Methods for Recommender Systems
contributions: Explains why sampled recommendation metrics can differ from full-catalog evaluation.
limitations: Does not replace the mandated benchmark; conclusions must remain specific to its sampled HR@10 protocol.
